Subject: Adaptive tier bridge & feature-swap proposal

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the latency profile on the dedicated tier, but our CFO is nervous about a big step-up right away. Procurement asked if we can explore a short-term bridge package that lets us test higher throughput for 90 days, then either commit to Dedicated or gracefully revert to our current mid-tier without penalty.

Key questions from our side:
- Can seat/throughput credits from the bridge convert to a Dedicated commit if we convert?
- What does a downgrade look like if we decide not to convert after 90 days? Any prorated credits or rollback fees?
- Are there feature bundles (e.g., private VPC, audit logs) that can be toggled on/off during the trial, or do they require a full-tier change?

We have a broad procurement checklist and an initial budget range — Id like to get a clear write-up we can share with finance. Could you send a proposal and an OKR-aligned checklist for the 90-day pilot? Attaching our internal procurement contact in case they want to loop in legal.

Best,
Claire O'Neill
Head of AI Integrations, EonHealth

Subject: Re: Adaptive tier bridge & feature-swap proposal

Thanks Claire — great to hear you found the latency good. I pulled together an initial pilot structure and attached the pricing worksheet and a draft SOW for procurement to review. High-level proposal:

- 90-day Bridge Pack (pilot): transient Dedicated-like capacity (burst-capacity pool) with throughput credits.
  - Monthly billing for actual tokens and a fixed seat overlay for predictable runway.
  - Credits earned during the pilot are convertible toward a Dedicated 12-month commit at a conversion ratio we can fix up-front (example in worksheet).
- Downgrade path: if you choose not to convert, well apply any remaining credits as account credits over 6 months; no rollback fee for standard usage patterns. There are carve-outs if theres abusive sustained overprovisioning — weve called those out in the SOW.
- Feature toggles: Private VPC and audit logs can be enabled for the pilot as an add-on. Some enterprise-only features (HSM integrations) require a Private deployment baseline; we show that in the feature matrix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min alignment call with procurement to confirm what "convertible credit" means to finance (I can host).
2) Confirm the conversion ratio and the acceptable audit/evidence items for the pilot period.
3) Finalize SOW and approval path.

Ive ccd Aditya (pricing) and Monica (customer success) to own the conversion mechanics and onboarding. See attached: EonHealth-Pricing-Worksheets.xlsx and SOW-draft-v1.pdf.

If that looks okay I can prepare a tightened two-page summary for finance.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Hannah — thanks for the clear proposal. A few clarifying items from procurement and finance:

1) Conversion ratio: finance wants a locked-in conversion floor (e.g., 75% of pilot spend converts to committed capacity credits) so they dont lose runway if usage spikes during the pilot. Can Redwood offer a firm floor like that?
2) Downgrade timing: if we revert, will users lose any feature entitlements immediately or do they remain in read-only for the 6-month credit window? Our security team needs to ensure no data access regression.
3) Discounting: given the scope were evaluating, procurement is requesting a one-time onboarding credit (first-month invoice credit) and an introductory 10% volume discount if we convert to a 12-month commit within 120 days.

If you can confirm the floor conversion and the feature state during downgrade, procurement will draft their redlines and we can loop legal. Also adding a request: can you share a 2-line explanation we can put in the board packet for our CFO that summarizes risk and rollback exposure?

Thanks,
Claire

Subject: Fwd: Adaptive tier bridge & feature-swap proposal — procurement asks

Team — forwarding Claire's requests. Quick positions to agree before I respond:

- Conversion floor: procurement wants a 75% conversion floor. Im inclined to offer a 70% floor with a conditional uplift to 75% if they hit a usage threshold (e.g., sustained 80% average utilization over 60 days). That limits downside but gives EonHealth comfort. Thoughts?
- Downgrade feature state: security cares that things remain read-only for 6 months. We can promise data access remains intact but mark certain enterprise integrations (HSM, Private KMS) as disabled until commit. Need legal to confirm exact language.
- Discount/onboarding credit: can we provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to first-month bill and offer a 10% conversion discount if they convert within 120 days? Pricing impact estimate in worksheet: if we do both, net ARR impact is ~-4% on the modeled commit.

Proposed reply to Claire: confirm the conditional 75% conversion floor (70% guaranteed + 5% contingent on utilization), confirm read-only feature posture during downgrade, and agree the two commercial asks (onboarding credit + 10% conversion discount) pending final legal/SalesOps approval. Ill ask Aditya to sign off on the exact numbers and Marcus to note CS onboarding constraints.

Can we finalize a one-page CFO blurb I can include in my reply? Marcus/Aditya — tagging you for an approval thread so I can close this out by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Hannah
